items.title: Mississauga renters lose over $30,000 in alleged apartment fraud
items.summary: Police are reminding residents to verify the identity of prospective landlords and not feel pressured into signing online agreements or to transfer funds before doing due diligence. , in the alleged rental apartment fraud scheme. Peel Regional Police have issued arrest warrants for two suspects in connection to an alleged Mississauga apartment rental fraud scheme. According to police, at least eight people were defrauded for more than $30,000 combined and have neither received the promised accommodation nor the funds they paid for the rental unit. The scheme allegedly took place between January and February 2025, when units were advertised on social media platforms, according to investigators with Peel police’s fraud bureau. The victims turned out to view an apartment, where they met individuals who claimed to be current tenants. After signing rental agreements online, the victims sent funds via e-transfer to secure the units, the police said. On move-in day, the victims learned the unit was unavailable. They were unable to contact the individual who posed as the landlord at the time of the apartment viewing. , is wanted for fraud over $5,000 and possession of property obtained by crime. , is wanted for fraud over $5,000, according to a police release.

items.title: Ceremony will honour legacy of first Black police officer in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: An upcoming street dedication and ceremony will honour retired Sgt. Sgt. Lonsdale “Lonny” Blackett, who made history and had a storied career as first Black police officer in Brampton and Mississauga. Blackett was just one of two Black recruits in the first-ever class of Peel Regional Police officers in 1974, and was the only one of the pair to make it through training. In his 33-year career he faced racism both on and off the force, working first in Brampton’s 21 Division before going on to help enlist other minority officers as a recruiter. He also helped found the PRP Airport Division, where he assisted with the rescue of Air France Flight 358 that crashed at Pearson International Airport in 2005. com, recalling how he and another officer ran onto the burning aircraft to evacuate the crew and anyone who may have still been on board. After checking the plane, Blackett says the officers saw more smoke coming from the rear and ran from the plane, which exploded shortly after. All of the flight’s 309 passengers and crew survived the crash, and Blackett would receive a commendation for his efforts on the scene. The City of Brampton started the process of honouring Blackett with a street dedication in February, and is holding a ceremony later this month at Mississauga Road just south of Bovaird Drive West – the future home of what will be known as Lonsdale Blackett Way. The event will be a ceremonial dedication, as the street will be part of upcoming developments in the area and has yet to be built, the city says. Residents are invited to the celebration on Aug. m. , and parking will be limited.

items.title: New restaurant opens replacing popular eatery in Mississauga
items.summary: A new restaurant has opened in Mississauga, replacing a popular eatery that had been in business for over a decade. Pal’ Antojo Mexican Restaurant announced it has officially opened at 277 Queen St. , a space previously occupied by Border MX Mexican Grill. Border MX Mexican Grill quietly closed its doors late last year. Open since 2014, the restaurant was a popular local spot known for its open-air patio, live music nights and a wide variety of traditional and modern Mexican dishes. The closure came after a difficult stretch for the business. On Valentine’s Day 2025, a pipe burst overnight inside the restaurant, causing major water damage throughout the kitchen. They reopened in April 2025. In May this year, Pal’ Antojo Mexican Restaurant said they were getting the location at 277 Queen St. S. ready to open. In the meantime, they had their food truck open behind the business. Today, Pal’ Antojo announced it was now open. “The wait is over!

items.title: 8 people scammed in apartment rental scheme in Mississauga
items.summary: Two people are wanted by police after at least eight people were scammed in an apartment rental scheme in Mississauga. Investigators with the Fraud Bureau seek two suspects in connection with an apartment rental fraud scheme that allegedly victimized multiple individuals in Mississauga, Peel Regional Police said on Thursday. Apartment rental opportunities were advertised on social media between January and February 2025, police said. Victims said they went to an apartment and met people who claimed to be the current tenants. The victims then signed rental agreements online and sent money by e-transfer to secure the rental unit, police said. But when they arrived to move in, they discovered the unit was unavailable, and the individual posing as the landlord could no longer be contacted, police said. Investigators have identified at least eight victims with combined financial losses exceeding $30,000, police said. Police said none of the victims received the promised accommodations or had their money returned. Warrants have been issued for the arrest of two people.

items.title: Making Mississauga Connections in Niagara
items.summary: I recently took a camping trip over the long weekend in Niagara – and we weathered to torrential rain ok, perhaps just a bit muddier for the experience. Whenever I spend some time in a place away from home, my thoughts and eyes are always drawn to the history of the area that I am now visiting. Old buildings, road names, heritage markers, interpretive signs, museums and the like always capture my interest and curiosity, and in that process of relaxed exploration, I am drawn to seeing if I can find connections back to Mississauga. The link to home came out of nowhere. While spending some idle time in the campground, there was a distant rumble, almost imperceptible at first, but over the next few minutes, the volume of the rumble grew steadily louder. We started looking around, and then up, as the sound grew louder and louder. Then suddenly, there it was, flying majestically overhead and at a relatively low altitude – so low that we could clearly see the marking and propellers – it was a Lancaster Bomber! Seeing the plane that I know well through story and history in flight (it was only my second time seeing it in flight), was quite something to behold. My own family stopped to watch as well, and we reflected on its role in the war effort during the Second World War. While there are only two flying Lancasters left in the world today – one in Canada and one in England – 430 Lancaster Bombers were built by Victory Aircraft in Malton (now within Mississauga). DR GABRIEL MONTEMURRO GRAVESTONE, STREETSVILLE PUBLIC CEMETERY. The Lancaster Bomber (Avro Lancaster Mk. X, RCAF FM213) that we saw overhead is from the Canadian Warplane Heritage Museum in Mount Hope, Ontario. The plane was originally built at Victory Aircraft, rolling off the assembly line in July of 1945, and was retired in 1963.

items.title: Driver fatally shot during Toronto police investigation in Mississauga: SIU
items.summary: Ontario’s police watchdog is investigating a fatal shooting involving Toronto police officers in Mississauga. The Special Investigations Unit said the shooting unfolded overnight on Thursday in relation to a “person with a gun” investigation. The shooting involved one officer and the driver of a vehicle. m on Delfi Road in Mississauga, in the area of The Collegeway and Winston Churchill Boulevard. Five unmarked Toronto police vehicles were involved in the operation, with three of them colliding with the Mercedes, Monica Hudon, spokesperson for the SIU, said. SIU initially said that the investigation was in regard to a stolen vehicle, but Toronto police later clarified the investigation was related to a report of a person with a gun and that the Mercedes had not been reported stolen. Following the collision, an officer who was standing on the roadway shot at the Mercedes, striking the 19-year-old driver, Hudon said. He died at the scene. The three other occupants were taken into custody and were not physically injured. One Toronto police officer was taken to hospital with minor injuries following one of the collisions. Investigators recovered two firearms from inside the Mercedes, but Hudon said there is no indication there was an exchange of gunfire.
